original_question: Is every compact embedded constant-mean-curvature disk in R^3 with circular boundary necessarily either a planar disk or a spherical cap?
target_in_paper: Section 2 ("Part I: Circular boundary"), Problem 2.12 (4*): "Is a compact embedded cmc disk of R^3 spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?" This is the paper’s explicit two-hypothesis version of the main circular-boundary conjectures. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it has the correct ambient space R^3, compactness, embeddedness, constant mean curvature, disk topology, circular boundary, and the intended dichotomy "planar disk or spherical cap." It also lands on the narrower embedded-plus-disk question rather than the broader embedded-only or immersed-disk variants. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
missing_details: In the paper, "disk" is meant topologically: the surface is a topological disk, not just any compact surface with one boundary component. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

The official formulation says "spanning a circle"; by the notation in Section 1, this means the boundary map is a diffeomorphism from ∂Σ onto a round circle S^1 in R^3. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

To be fully stand-alone, the conclusion should say that Σ is either the planar disk bounded by that circle or a spherical cap having that same circle as boundary. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))

The paper treats this as distinct from the broader embedded-only problem (Problem 2.1 / Conjecture 1) and from the immersed-disk problem (Problem 2.8 / Conjecture 2), so that distinction should be kept explicit. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
refined_question: Let Σ ⊂ R^3 be a compact embedded surface of constant mean curvature, homeomorphic to the closed 2-disk, such that its boundary ∂Σ is a round circle. Must Σ be either the planar disk bounded by ∂Σ or a spherical cap with boundary ∂Σ? ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
equivalent_formulation: Is a compact embedded cmc disk of R^3 spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap? ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
justification: The draft is not best matched by the paper’s main embedded-only conjecture/problem, because it adds the disk hypothesis; nor is it the immersed-disk problem, because it keeps embeddedness. Section 1 first isolates three separate boundary analogues of Alexandrov/Hopf/Barbosa–do Carmo: embedded, topological disk, and stable. Then Section 2 explicitly says that an easier route is to assume two of these three hypotheses, and it formulates exactly the embedded-plus-disk question as Problem 2.12. So the sharp paper-faithful target is Problem 2.12. ([digibug.ugr.es](https://digibug.ugr.es/bitstream/handle/10481/110069/conm16439-offprints.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1))
